# @horizon-republic/nominal-types

> Runtime-validated nominal types for TypeScript. A type is a class with a rule: `new Email(text)` checks the text once, and every `Email` you hold is valid. Types don't mix at compile time, even when they wrap the same kind of value. Every type is a Standard Schema and a Standard JSON Schema, and adapters connect types to ArkType, NestJS, class-validator and Swagger.

## Defaults to follow

- Check a request body, a message or a config with `objectOf({ field: Type, list: schemaOf(Type).array(), maybe: schemaOf(Type).optional() })`. No other library needed; every field comes out as an instance; unknown keys are dropped (`.strict()` refuses them). In a project that already uses ArkType, or for unions, recursion and transforms, use `fromArk(type({ field: toArk(Type) }))` from `@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/arktype`.
- Read configuration with `class Config extends Nominal('app.Config', objectOf({ PORT: Port, DEBUG: AnyBoolean }).fromEnv())` and `new Config(process.env)`: fields with a text form are read from strings, other variables are dropped, and one `NominalError` lists every bad variable.
- Make a value object of several fields with `class Stay extends Nominal('booking.Stay', objectOf({ … }, constraint))`: getters per field (`stay.guests`), `stay.copyWith({ guests: 3 })` returns a checked copy and throws `NominalError` when a rule breaks.
- Name the schema and its value type the same: `export const X = fromArk(…); export type X = ValueOf<typeof X>;`.
- Use `Type.parse(input)` for input that may be wrong; it returns `{ ok: true, value }` or `{ ok: false, issues }`. Use `new Type(value)` only where a bad value is a bug; it throws `NominalError`.
- Write a rule across fields once with `constraint()` and attach it: `objectOf({ … }, rule)`, `fromArk(type, rule)`, `constrainArk(type, rule)` for a nested ArkType object, or `Nominal('Name', rule)`.
- In NestJS, check route parameters and query values with `NominalPipe` from `@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/nest`, or `{ schema: Type }` on NestJS 12.
- Use `@NominalField()` from `@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/class-validator` only in projects that already use class-validator.
- Name types with the part of the system in front and a dot: `Nominal('billing.InvoiceNumber', …)`, class named like the last part (`class InvoiceNumber`). Names allow letters, digits, `_` and `-` in each part; `/` and spaces throw. Built-in types are named `nominal.Email`, `nominal.Uuid` and so on.
- In Zod use `toZod(Type)` for fields and `constrainZod(object, ...constraints)` (`/adapters/zod`); in Valibot `toValibot(Type)` and `constrainValibot(object, ...constraints)` (`/adapters/valibot`). Adapter functions are named verb + library: `to…` (our type into the library), `constrain…` (rules onto the library's object), `fromArk` (an ArkType schema back to instances).
- Store instances with `p.type(toMikroOrm(Type))` (`/adapters/mikro-orm`), `@Column(toTypeOrm(Type))` (`/adapters/typeorm`), `customType<DrizzleColumn<typeof Type>>(toDrizzle(Type))` (`/adapters/drizzle`) or `toSequelize(Type)` as a model attribute (`/adapters/sequelize`; its `where` takes stored values, not instances). The column type comes from the nominal type; reads are checked (`trusted: true` skips it); `serialize` chooses what is stored and also runs on query values.
- Use `schemaOf(Type)` inside libraries that have no adapter; inside ArkType prefer `toArk(Type)`, which is about 20 times faster.

## Core API

```ts
import { constraint, Email, Nominal, PositiveInteger, schemaOf, Uuid } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types';

export class OrderNumber extends Nominal('sales.OrderNumber', /^ORD-\d{8}$/u) {
  get year(): number {
    return Number(this.value.slice(4, 8));
  }
}

export class ExpressOrderNumber extends OrderNumber.subtype('sales.ExpressOrderNumber', /^ORD-\d{4}9/u) {}

OrderNumber.parse('42'); // { ok: false, issues: [{ message: 'must be matched by ^ORD-\d{8}$ (was "42")' }] }
new OrderNumber('ORD-20261007').value; // 'ORD-20261007'

schemaOf(Uuid).array({ min: 1 }).optional(); // a Standard Schema for an optional, non-empty list of Uuid

export const withinCapacity = constraint(
  { guests: PositiveInteger, capacity: PositiveInteger },
  ({ guests, capacity }) => guests <= capacity || 'must not exceed the capacity',
  { path: 'guests' },
);
```

- A rule is a `RegExp`, `matching(pattern, description)`, `satisfying(guard, description, jsonSchema)` or any synchronous Standard Schema (ArkType, Zod, Valibot).
- `subtype(name, rule?)` makes a narrower type that passes where its parent is expected. `variant(name, rule)` makes a sibling that passes for neither.
- Instances compare by value: `end > start`, `Number(count)`, `` `${email}` ``. Compare an instance with a plain number through `.value`: `count.value <= 10`. An instance holding an object throws a `TypeError` in `>` or `+`; compare its fields through `.value`.
- An object or array value is frozen; the input is copied first. `equals()` compares by value within one line of types.

## ArkType adapter

```ts
import { type } from 'arktype';
import { constrainArk, toArk, fromArk } from '@horizon-republic/nominal-types/adapters/arktype';

const Stay = constrainArk(
  type({ guests: toArk(PositiveInteger), capacity: toArk(PositiveInteger) }),
  withinCapacity,
);

export const CreateBooking = fromArk(
  type({
    id: toArk(Uuid),
    email: type('string.trim').pipe(toArk(Email)),
    'backup?': toArk(Email).or('null'),
    stays: Stay.array(),
  }),
);

CreateBooking.parse(body);
// { ok: true, value: { id: Uuid, email: Email, stays: [{ guests: PositiveInteger, … }] } }
// { ok: false, issues: [{ message: 'must not exceed the capacity', path: ['stays', 0, 'guests'] }] }
```

- `toArk(Type)` is a field, `constrainArk(type, ...constraints)` an object with rules, `fromArk(type, ...constraints)` the whole schema.
- Supported around `toArk()`: optional keys, `.or('null')`, arrays, tuples, records, unions told apart by type or by a literal field, morphs that end in `toArk()`. `fromArk()` throws a `TypeError` for a morph after `toArk()` and for unions it can't tell apart.
- The result is a Standard Schema with JSON Schema for `draft-2020-12`, `draft-07` and `openapi-3.0`; NestJS 12 takes it as `@Body({ schema: CreateBooking })`.

## Built-in types

Strings: `AnyString`, `Email`, `Uuid`, `Url`, `HttpUrl`. Numbers: `AnyNumber`, `FiniteNumber`, `Integer`, `Float32`, `PositiveNumber`, `NegativeNumber`, `NonNegativeNumber`, `NonPositiveNumber`, `PositiveInteger`, `NegativeInteger`, `NonNegativeInteger`, `NonPositiveInteger`, `Int8`, `Int16`, `Int32`, `Uint8`, `Uint16`, `Uint32`. Big integers: `AnyBigInt`, `PositiveBigInt`, `NegativeBigInt`, `NonNegativeBigInt`, `NonPositiveBigInt`, `Int64`, `Uint64` (written to JSON as decimal strings). Booleans: `AnyBoolean`.
